per_question.question: What are the entrance, continued service, and discharge criteria for outpatient behavioral health services in NC Medicaid?
per_question.agent_answer:
For **NC Medicaid outpatient behavioral health services**, the governing rule is that the service must first meet the policy’s general coverage standards, and then the beneficiary must meet the more specific **entrance, continued service, and discharge criteria** for outpatient behavioral health. Under the current **8C policy, effective April 15, 2025**, no separate amendment was identified in the amendment record returned for this document. [8C, Outpatient Behavioral Health Services Provided by Direct-Enrolled Providers](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8c-outpatient-behavioral-health-services-provided-direct-enrolled-providers/download?attachment)

## General coverage rule
A service is covered only if it is:

- **individualized, specific, and consistent with the beneficiary’s symptoms or confirmed diagnosis**, and not more than the beneficiary needs;
- **able to be safely furnished**, with no equally effective and more conservative or less costly treatment available statewide; and
- **not furnished primarily for the convenience** of the beneficiary, caregiver, or provider.  
  [8C, Outpatient Behavioral Health Services Provided by Direct-Enrolled Providers](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8c-outpatient-behavioral-health-services-provided-direct-enrolled-providers/download?attachment)

Also, the service is **not covered** if the beneficiary does not meet the policy’s Section 3 criteria, among other general exclusions. [8C, Outpatient Behavioral Health Services Provided by Direct-Enrolled Providers](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8c-outpatient-behavioral-health-services-provided-direct-enrolled-providers/download?attachment)

## Entrance criteria
For outpatient behavioral health services, the beneficiary must meet these entrance criteria:

- have a current **DSM-5 diagnosis**;
- present **behavioral, psychological, or biological dysfunction and functional impairment** that are consistent with and associated with that diagnosis;
- if a **higher level of care is indicated** but unavailable, or the beneficiary is refusing it, outpatient services may be provided until that higher level of care is available or to support the beneficiary in participating in it;
- be **capable of developing skills** to manage symptoms, make behavioral changes, and respond favorably to therapeutic interventions; and
- have **no evidence that alternative interventions would be more effective**, based on North Carolina community practice standards.  
  [8C, Outpatient Behavioral Health Services Provided by Direct-Enrolled Providers](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8c-outpatient-behavioral-health-services-provided-direct-enrolled-providers/download?attachment)

## Continued service criteria
The policy text says continued services require:

### First, at least one of these:
- the desired outcome or level of functioning **has not been restored, improved, or sustained** within the timeframe in the treatment plan;
- the beneficiary **continues to be at risk for relapse** based on current clinical assessment and history; or
- the beneficiary’s functional gains are **tenuous**.

### And, in addition, at least one of these:
- the beneficiary has **achieved current treatment-plan goals**, but **additional goals are indicated** as shown by documented symptoms; or
- the beneficiary is **making satisfactory progress toward meeting goals**, and there is documentation supporting that.

That is the text I could verify from the current policy section. The retrieved section appears to end mid-sentence after “there is documentation that supports that,” so I cannot verify any additional wording that may follow in the full source beyond what was returned here.  
[8C, Outpatient Behavioral Health Services Provided by Direct-Enrolled Providers](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8c-outpatient-behavioral-health-services-provided-direct-enrolled-providers/download?attachment)

## Discharge criteria
The beneficiary meets discharge criteria if **any** of the following applies:

- the beneficiary’s **level of functioning has improved** with respect to the goals in the treatment plan;
- the beneficiary or legally responsible person **no longer wishes to receive** the services; or
- the beneficiary, because of current presentation and **failure to improve despite treatment-plan modifications**, needs a **more appropriate best practice or evidence-based treatment modality** based on North Carolina community practice standards.  
  [8C, Outpatient Behavioral Health Services Provided by Direct-Enrolled Providers](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8c-outpatient-behavioral-health-services-provided-direct-enrolled-providers/download?attachment)

## Documentation requirement
The provider’s clinical documentation must include **documentation of entrance criteria, continued service criteria, and discharge criteria** in the service record.  
[8C, Outpatient Behavioral Health Services Provided by Direct-Enrolled Providers](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8c-outpatient-behavioral-health-services-provided-direct-enrolled-providers/download?attachment)
